capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

For the first statement, use the normal-form interpretation of `Word.equivPair`: every word uniquely decomposes into an initial factor from `M i` followed by a word whose first index is not `i`. Since `p.tail` already has first index different from `i` by `p.fstIdx_ne`, its initial `M i` factor is `1`; hence its image is exactly `Pair.mk 1 p.tail p.fstIdx_ne`.

For the second, use the universal property of the indexed coproduct. The lifted endomorphism agrees with the identity on every canonical generator:
\[
(\operatorname{lift}(\operatorname{of}))(\operatorname{of}_i(x))=\operatorname{of}_i(x).
\]
Then coproduct homomorphism extensionality—or equivalently uniqueness in the `lift` equivalence—shows that this endomorphism is `MonoidHom.id`. Thus the proof is organized as constructor, normal-form simplification for the first component, and generatorwise extensionality for the second.
